name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: class 1 and class 2 (throttle) stop at 20 mph, class 3 (pedal assist) at 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; class 2 can propel it without pedaling and stops at 20 mph; class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph (Mississippi Code §63-3-103)
The motor must disengage when the brakes are applied (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
Riders of class 3 must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
Must not be tampered with or modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512) (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle and is not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration, title, plate or insurance (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
Not an off-road vehicle, dirt bike or all-terrain vehicle under state law (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, highways, bike lanes and bicycle or multi-use paths (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
A municipality, local authority or state agency may ban class 1 or 2 from a bicycle or multi-use path only after notice and a public hearing, for safety or legal reasons (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
A municipality, local authority or state agency may ban class 3 from any bicycle or multi-use path, with no hearing needed (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed (Mississippi Code §63-3-1315)
